newsitem.title: USA: CME cattle futures end higher but off peaks.
newsitem.headline: CME cattle futures end higher but off peaks.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed higher, but speculative and commercial selling trimmed gains amid ideas meat packers will be reluctant to bid cash prices higher during the holiday week, traders said.
Feeder cattle closed with strong gains, but down from the limit gains and contract highs posted early in the session.
A smaller-than-expected U.S. hog supply motivated buying as traders believed beef will be price-competitive with pork.

"Beef is competing extremely well with pork right now and with the pork supply expected to be down the price relationship should continue to favor beef," said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst with Brock and Associates.

Feeder cattle bounded sharply higher near midsession when CBOT corn futures were down slightly. A lower-than-expected U.S. corn acreage estimate in USDA's acreage report released early Monday had cattle traders expecting much higher corn prices, which would mean higher feed costs and less demand for feeder cattle.
CBOT December corn futures closed up 2-3/4 cents at $2.38-1/4 cents per bushel, but slipped to a contract low of 2.33-3/4 cents earlier in the session.

Gains in feeder cattle were attributed to higher cash prices at recent auctions, the product of ranchers having lush pastures that discouraged selling feeders to feedlots, traders said. As a result, feedlots have to pay higher prices for the limited supply.
At Oklahoma City's Monday auction feeder steers traded $2.00 higher, with 700- to 800-lb feeders trading from $80.50 to $84.50 per cwt.
Feeder cattle closed up 0.350 to 0.900 cent with August up 0.475 at 80.875 cents. Contract highs were set in all contracts with August's contract high at 81.800.
Live cattle closed unchanged to up 0.750 cent with August unchanged at 64.450 cents per lb.
Contract highs were set in February 1998 live cattle, 72.60 cents; April 1998, 74.500; June 1998, 70.95; and August 1998, 70.300 cent.
